issue.title: fix(runtime-core): watching multiple values - handle `undefined` as initial values (fix: #5032)

repository.name: core
repository.description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.

issue.body:
We currently have an empty array as the intial `oldValue` for a watcher that watches multiple values.

This does fail for an edge case where we watch multiple values and all of them are initially undefined, and trigger the watcher immediately.

We can solve this by settting the initial `oldValue` to an array filled with `INITIAL_WATCHER_VALUE`

fix: #5032

issue.title: Fix use of `undefined` and `displayValue` in Combobox

repository.name: headlessui
repository.description: Completely unstyled, fully accessible UI components, designed to integrate beautifully with Tailwind CSS.

issue.body:
When the combobox box is given a v-model ref that is `undefined` we do not call `displayValue` and can end up displaying the string `undefined`. This is actually a bug in Vue itself (https://github.com/vuejs/core/issues/5032) but we can work around this by passing a dummy ref that has a defined value. This allows `immediate` to work as expected.

Fixes #1861

issue.title: immediate didn't work in `watch([()=>undefined]`

repository.name: core

issue.body:
### Vue version

3.2.40

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://sfc.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

```
const a = ref(undefined);

watch([a], ()=>{
  console.log('no print, immediate didn't work')
}, {immediate:true});
```

### What is expected?

immediate:true working

### What is actually happening?

immediate:true didn't work
